name: MCP9808 precision temperature sensor
description: Microchip digital temperature sensor, -40 to 125 °C with ±0.25 °C typical (±0.5 °C max from -20 to 100 °C) accuracy and 0.0625 °C resolution, on an I2C bus. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit MCP9808 High Accuracy I2C Temperature Sensor Breakout (#1782, 8-pin: VDD, GND, SCL, SDA, Alert, A0, A1, A2), I2C address 0x18 (0x18–0x1F with A0–A2).
eli5: A very accurate thermometer chip your board can ask for the temperature over two wires.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply and logic level, 2.7–5.5 V (use the microcontroller's 3.3 V)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10k pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10k pull-up to VDD on the board)

pins.name: Alert
pins.description: Alert/thermostat output, open-drain (needs a pull-up); not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: Adafruit MCP9808 I2C temperature sensor breakout
buildNotes: Check the chip first: register 0x06 reads 0x0054 (Microchip) and the upper byte of register 0x07 reads 0x04.
Temperature is register 0x05 (16 bits, MSB first): mask off bits 15–13 (alert flags), bit 12 is the sign, bits 11–0 are 0.0625 °C steps. T = (raw & 0x0FFF) / 16, minus 256 when bit 12 is set.
The power-up resolution is 0.0625 °C with a 250 ms conversion; reading faster just repeats the last result.
A0, A1 and A2 have pull-downs: leave them unconnected for 0x18, tie them to VDD to add 1, 2 or 4 (up to eight sensors on one bus).
Keep the board away from the regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air nearby.

driver.code:
# MCP9808 precision temperature sensor (Microchip DS20005095B), MicroPython driver.
# 16-bit registers, MSB first. Ambient temperature register TA (0x05):
#   bits 15..13 = alert flags (TA >= TCRIT, TA > TUPPER, TA < TLOWER), bit 12 = sign,
#   bits 11..0 = temperature in 0.0625 degC steps (two's complement with the sign bit).
import time

_REG_CONFIG = 0x01
_REG_TA = 0x05
_REG_MANUF_ID = 0x06
_REG_DEVICE_ID = 0x07
_REG_RESOLUTION = 0x08

# Resolution register value -> typical conversion time (ms), datasheet Register 5-7
_TCONV_MS = {0: 30, 1: 65, 2: 130, 3: 250}


class MCP9808:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x18):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        manuf = self._read16(_REG_MANUF_ID)
        dev = self._read16(_REG_DEVICE_ID) >> 8
        if manuf != 0x0054 or dev != 0x04:
            raise OSError('MCP9808 not found at 0x%02X (manufacturer 0x%04X, device 0x%02X)' % (addr, manuf, dev))

    def _read16(self, reg):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def _write16(self, reg, value):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([(value >> 8) & 0xFF, value & 0xFF]))

    def set_resolution(self, res):
        """0 = 0.5 C (30 ms), 1 = 0.25 C (65 ms), 2 = 0.125 C (130 ms), 3 = 0.0625 C (250 ms, power-up default)."""
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_RESOLUTION, bytes([res & 0x03]))
        time.sleep_ms(_TCONV_MS[res & 0x03])

    def shutdown(self, off=True):
        """Set or clear CONFIG bit 8 (SHDN). In shutdown the chip draws about 0.1 uA and stops converting."""
        cfg = self._read16(_REG_CONFIG)
        cfg = (cfg | 0x0100) if off else (cfg & ~0x0100)
        self._write16(_REG_CONFIG, cfg)
        if not off:
            time.sleep_ms(250)  # wait one full conversion before reading

    def temperature(self):
        """Ambient temperature in degC (datasheet Equation 5-1)."""
        raw = self._read16(_REG_TA) & 0x1FFF  # mask the three alert flag bits
        t = (raw & 0x0FFF) / 16
        if raw & 0x1000:  # sign bit: TA < 0 degC
            t -= 256
        return t

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mcp9808 import MCP9808

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = MCP9808(i2c)  # address 0x18 with A0/A1/A2 unconnected
time.sleep_ms(300)  # first 0.0625 C conversion takes 250 ms after power-up
while True:
    print('T=%.2fC' % sensor.temperature())
    time.sleep(1)
